body:
So the important point seems to be that https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#destroy-a-child-navigable will only be invoked from https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#html-element-removing-steps for elements that contain a navigable. So the question is "does anything invoke those steps when closing a tab?"

The action when you close a tab is defined in https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#nav-traversal-ui:close-a-top-level-traversable, which calls https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#close-a-top-level-traversable and then https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#unload-a-document-and-its-descendants , which calls https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#unload-a-document for each descendant document. That runs https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#unloading-document-cleanup-steps which doesn't invoke the "HTML element removal steps" and then https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#destroy-a-document which runs the "unloading document cleanup steps" again(!), but doesn't run the "HTML element removal steps". Then eventually we end up back at "unload a document and its descendants", which _for the top-level traversable only_ was passed an `afterAllUnloads` which calls https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#destroy-a-top-level-traversable

So I think it's correct that we would end up invoking the BiDi event in the following cases:
* When a top-level traversable is destroyed
* When an iframe is removed from the document
* When an embed element is (re?)used, but there's no plugin 
* When an object element is (re?)used to render an image
* When an object element's fallback is used
* When a frame element is removed

The object/embed cases are probably not that relevant. So I think this makes sense (but I also think the frequent HTML pattern of passing round sets of steps to call actually makes it quite difficult to tell if something is actually called recursively or not because it means that the real call sites are not actually linked).
